state:
Goal `core-test-1-2`, stage 2. `Core\Test::advance` and `Core\Test::answerHttp` have every proof.
`answerHttp` has `about.md`, three examples, one attack, a bench with a recorded figure in
`docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and the Rust test
`answer_http_takes_every_status_a_status_line_carries_and_a_refused_answer_arms_nothing`. Its attack
found no bug. `Core\Test`'s class card is at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:560`, so `help` passes for
every member of the class.

Every `Core\Test` member's proofs run under `nvs run`, not `nvs test` (see the playbook bullet in
*Writing a test case*). `bun nv try <files>` runs them that way before blessing. `answerHttp` and
`answerSocket` work at the top level of a program, with no `#[Test]` class. A bench needs
`bun nv proofs --record-perf --only '<member>'`. Its first release build may exit 255 with no error;
the second run succeeded.

items.text: **`Core\Test::answerSocket`**: about, 3 examples, attack, Rust `covers:` test, bench. It uses `answerHttp`'s answer table, so the Rust test can follow `answer_http_takes_every_status_a_status_line_carries_and_a_refused_answer_arms_nothing` and read `ctx.faked_http_mut().socket_for(url)`. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:780`

**`Core\Test::assertCalled`** and **`Core\Test::assertNeverCalled`**: the same proofs. Both read the doubles' call record, so they share a Rust test module. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:4588`
